source: Lee, McLeish, Goldstein, Fanti (2026) Do Language Models Need Sleep? Offline Recurrence for Improved Online Inference
finding: A hybrid model periodically converts evicted context into fast weights with N offline recurrent passes (a sleep phase). Hybrid SSM-attention models without sleep fail as reasoning depth grows even when memory load is fixed; more passes help most on deep items.
numbers: Rule 110 task, sequence length fixed at 100: 4-layer GDN-attention hybrid accuracy drops as depth t rises; plain transformer is at chance (25%) under hard eviction.
limits: Needs architecture change and training; wake-time answer is a single pass. Synthetic tasks plus GSM-Infinite. Not a prompting method.
agent_relevance: Consolidation is computation, not just storage: extra offline passes beat one summary pass.

source: Lee, McLeish, Goldstein, Fanti (2026) Do Language Models Need Sleep? Offline Recurrence for Improved Online Inference (GSM-Infinite, pretrained models)
finding: With pretrained Jet and Ouro models, more sleep loops raise accuracy on harder 6- and 8-operation problems; easy problems saturate.
limits: Gain on 8-op for Jet is small. Fine-tuning needed. Point estimates in text.
agent_relevance: Offline work pays most when later questions need multi-step reasoning over stored material.

source: Lee, McLeish, Goldstein, Fanti (2026) Do Language Models Need Sleep? Offline Recurrence for Improved Online Inference (sliding-window eviction)
finding: With a window far smaller than the sequence, loops also help retrieval and compression, not only reasoning.
numbers: Ouro 1.4B, L=512, 2-op problems: accuracy 0.596 (no loop) to 0.905 with loops (paper: 52% improvement).
limits: Fine-tuned on this task family; no human comparison.
agent_relevance: Offline passes can repair lossy compression of old context.

source: Xie (2026) Learning to Forget: Sleep-Inspired Memory Consolidation for Resolving Proactive Interference in LLMs (SleepGate)
finding: SleepGate adds a learned sleep cycle over the KV cache (conflict tagging, forgetting gate, merging of survivors). On a proactive-interference benchmark it beats five baselines by a large margin in a toy setting.
numbers: 4-layer 793K-parameter transformer: 99.5% retrieval at PI depth 5, 97.0% at depth 10; all five baselines (full KV cache, sliding window, H2O, StreamingLLM, decay-only) below 18%. Full KV cache only 8.0% at n=1.
limits: Proof of concept, tiny model, synthetic task, no human data, no frontier model. Preprint.
agent_relevance: Active forgetting of superseded entries is part of consolidation: stale memory entries must be superseded, not only added.

source: Xie (2026) Learning to Forget: Sleep-Inspired Memory Consolidation for Resolving Proactive Interference in LLMs (SleepGate) (depth limits)
finding: Benefit collapses at high interference depth: the gate cannot separate many similar entries.
numbers: 97.0% at n=10, 73.5% at n=15, 16.5% at n=30; stale retrieval rate 62% at n=30. Sleep overhead 15.6%.
limits: Authors list depth saturation and over-forgetting risk (soft biasing limits it).
agent_relevance: Consolidating many near-duplicate episodes can fail; keep raw episodes for recovery.

source: Behrouz, Hashemi, Javanmard, Mirrokni (2026) Language Models Need Sleep: Learning to Self-Modify and Consolidate Memories (continual language learning)
finding: Sleep = knowledge seeding (distill small self into larger network) then dreaming (RL-made synthetic curriculum). Sleep-time consolidation stops in-context learning from collapsing when two new languages are learned in sequence.
numbers: MTOB plus Manchu translation: under sequential learning ICL drops sharply to near pretrained behaviour; Hope-3 (more consolidation stages) nearly recovers single-language chrF. SFT and Cartridges forgot at least one language.
limits: Needs weight updates and RL. Exact chrF only in a figure. Single group, preprint.
agent_relevance: Replay or rehearsal of new knowledge prevents loss, but needs training.

source: Behrouz, Hashemi, Javanmard, Mirrokni (2026) Language Models Need Sleep: Learning to Self-Modify and Consolidate Memories (math reasoning)
finding: Sleep beats SFT, GRPO and on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) on AIME/HMMT, but margins over OPSD are small.
numbers: Qwen3-8B AIME-24: base 73.8, GRPO 76.4, OPSD 76.6, Sleep 79.2; AIME-25 69.0 vs OPSD 67.4; HMMT-25 46.1 vs 45.1. Qwen3-1.7B AIME-24: OPSD 51.6, Sleep 53.2.
limits: Gains of 1-3 points; average@16; no seed variance in the text.
agent_relevance: Weight-level consolidation helps modestly; not usable in our no-training scaffold.

source: Behrouz, Hashemi, Javanmard, Mirrokni (2026) Language Models Need Sleep: Learning to Self-Modify and Consolidate Memories (knowledge incorporation, few-shot ARC)
finding: Dreaming (self-generated synthetic rehearsal data) carries knowledge incorporation; removing it collapses scores. Few-shot ARC subset: Sleep 80% vs SEAL 72.5%, TTT 10%, ICL 0%.
numbers: Ablation: removing Dreaming gives 35.7 and 36.2 versus about 47-49 for full Sleep (no-context SQuAD accuracy). ARC: 11 train tasks, 8 held-out tasks only.
limits: Tiny ARC sample (8 tasks). Authors' own setup.
agent_relevance: Generative replay (self-made variants) does the work; consolidation without it does not.

source: Ye et al. (2026) Auto-Dreamer: Learning Offline Memory Consolidation for Language Agents
finding: A learned offline consolidator rewrites a region of the memory bank into a smaller abstract set, using tools and source-trajectory links, trained with GRPO. CLS-inspired: fast per-session write, slow cross-session consolidation.
numbers: ScienceWorld success 41.1% vs 34.1% best baseline (UMEM), +7.0 pts; +10.2 over prompted ReasoningBank (30.9%). ALFWorld 60.2%. Control study: ALFWorld 72.7% (ExpeL 70.1), ScienceWorld 44.3% (Mem0 42.0).
limits: Point estimates, no seed or task-order variance (authors admit small ALFWorld margins). Trained on ScienceWorld only.
agent_relevance: Closest published analogue of our offline job turning episodes into rules; acquisition and consolidation kept separate.

source: Ye et al. (2026) Auto-Dreamer: Learning Offline Memory Consolidation for Language Agents (ablation)
finding: Most compaction comes from region rewriting alone, before any training. Training adds success but can lose specifics.
numbers: Untrained pipeline gives 6x-11x smaller bank than writer-only. GRPO adds +9.7 pp ScienceWorld, +5.7 pp WebArena, +1.0 pp ALFWorld. Hurts the look_at_obj_in_light family (location details lost under abstraction); excluding it, margin +4.9 pp on other five.
limits: Single run; ALFWorld gain small and bank grows.
agent_relevance: Abstraction erases location-specific details: consolidation needs a way to keep exceptions.

source: Zeng et al. (2026) Use and Disuse: Intent-Structured Experience Consolidation for Memory and Learning in LLM Agents (Hippocam)
finding: Hippocam consolidates finished intents, recursively abstracts old history, and re-consolidates memories when recalled; raw interactions kept for drill-down.
numbers: ScienceWorld transfer: 78.9% mean progress, +30.1 pp over Plain, +16.2 over ACE. LoCoMo 77.6%, +10.1 pp over A-Mem. 64k MemoryAgentBench: 41.0% with recall, 27.0% with recall disabled.
limits: Single runs. Some baselines win elsewhere (A-Mem on ScienceWorld 87.2%, Letta on StreamBench 81.3%). Interleaved tasks cost 23.1 pp on GoodAI.
agent_relevance: Keep raw episodes plus abstractions; the 14-point drop without recall shows consolidation alone loses information.

source: Dai et al. (2026) RecMem: Recurrence-based Memory Consolidation for Efficient and Effective Long-Running LLM Agents
finding: Consolidate only when similar interactions recur (a replay-priority rule), not on every turn. Cuts cost without losing accuracy.
numbers: LoCoMo: 193.2K construction tokens vs 1520.8K (Mem0) and 1459.9K (A-Mem), 87.3% and 86.8% fewer. LongMemEval-S: 77.5% fewer than Mem0, 71.1% fewer than A-Mem. LoCoMo ablation overall: 81.10 full vs 70.58 to 79.94 for ablations; 51.88 worst.
limits: Authors say it does not win every category; thresholds tuned per benchmark.
agent_relevance: Trigger consolidation by recurrence of similar episodes, a code-side rule, not a model opinion.

source: Song et al. (2026) Retrieval-Driven Memory Reconsolidation for Long-Term LLM Agents (REALM)
finding: Reconsolidation after retrieval (memory updated when used) adds a consistent gain to a graph memory.
numbers: Average accuracy LoCoMo 73.96 to 75.97 (+2.01), LongMemEval 62.98 to 65.11 (+2.13). Largest category gains: LongMemEval single-session preference +6.66, LoCoMo open/update +5.21, multi-hop +4.97.
limits: Gains about 2 points; single runs; reconsolidation differs from slow-wave replay.
agent_relevance: Update memories at the time they are recalled; cheap and measurable.

source: Kyrkewood (2026) The Sleeping Agent: What Gist-Based Context Compression Loses and Why
finding: Sleep-inspired gist compression beats truncation on multi-hop and single-hop but fails on temporal questions because the gist drops dates. A one-sentence prompt fix recovers it.
numbers: LoCoMo, 1,501 questions, Claude Sonnet 4.6, temp 0: SWC-Temporal 0.468, SWC-Full 0.379, sliding window 0.238, truncation 0.171; full-context ceiling 0.706 (299 q). Temporal expression preservation 3.05% to 62.39%; temporal accuracy +0.314 [0.254, 0.375], n=315. SWC-Full temporal 0.156 vs single-hop 0.459.
limits: Single independent author; LoCoMo only; full-context reference on only 2 conversations.
agent_relevance: Gist consolidation drops time and place: schema extraction must carry dates and exceptions as required slots.

source: Lin et al. (2025) Sleep-time Compute: Beyond Inference Scaling at Test-time
finding: Precomputing inferences over a known context while idle lets the model answer later queries with less test-time compute.
numbers: About 5x fewer test-time tokens for same accuracy on Stateful GSM-Symbolic (P1+P2) and Stateful AIME (60 questions); scaling sleep compute adds up to +13% (GSM) and +18% (AIME); per-query cost up to 2.5x lower on Multi-Query GSM-Symbolic.
limits: At high test-time budgets the test-time-only baseline slightly beats sleep-time (authors guess distracting text). Gain depends on how predictable the query is from context.
agent_relevance: An offline pass is worth it only when future questions are predictable; otherwise skip.

source: Bazhenov, Delanois, Krishnan (2026) Not Just After One: Sleep-Inspired Replay Prevents Catastrophic Forgetting After Sequential Tasks
finding: One sleep (SRC) after several tasks restores performance on all earlier tasks, but recovery shrinks as more tasks pile up before sleep.
numbers: 5-task MNIST-style protocol: after task 5, earlier tasks scored 0.00 without sleep; SRC restored roughly 0.33 to 0.75 per task (mean about 0.53; read from a garbled table).
limits: Small fully connected nets, image tasks, no LLM. Preprint; I read only the early part and the table is garbled.
agent_relevance: Delaying consolidation across many episodes loses recoverable detail; consolidate in batches.

source: Tadros, Krishnan, Ramyaa, Bazhenov (2022) Sleep-like unsupervised replay reduces catastrophic forgetting in artificial neural networks
finding: Sleep Replay Consolidation (noisy input, local Hebbian updates in a spiking version of the net) recovers old tasks after sequential training.
numbers: CUB-200: without sleep first task 5%, second 95%; with SRC 63.2% and 45.4%. CIFAR-10: 44% with SRC vs 19% control (5 trials, varied init and task order).
limits: Small networks; below the parallel-training upper bound; complementary to small rehearsal (0.75% of old data).
agent_relevance: Unsupervised replay of structure, no stored examples, can preserve old knowledge; analogue is replaying summaries.

source: Arani, Sarfraz, Zonooz (2022) Learning Fast, Learning Slow: CLS-ER
finding: Two slow EMA-weighted semantic models (plastic and stable) plus an episodic buffer implement complementary learning systems; the stable model is used at inference.
numbers: Largest case: Seq-Tiny-ImageNet with 200-sample buffer, gain of 176% over ER and 114% over DER++. Gap grows with more tasks and harder data.
limits: Needs a replay buffer; gains largest at small memory; in some settings other methods do as well.
agent_relevance: Computational CLS works as continual learning; slow and fast stores apply to memory banks.

source: Park et al. (2023) Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
finding: Reflection (periodic synthesis of memories into higher-level statements, triggered when summed importance passes a threshold) is one of three components; removing components lowers believability.
numbers: 100 Prolific raters, TrueSkill: ablations scored 26.88, 25.64, human crowdworkers 22.95, no memory/planning/reflection 21.21; prior-work condition vs full architecture d=8.16. Kruskal-Wallis H(4)=150.29, p<0.001.
limits: Believability rating, not task accuracy; reflection effect is not isolated from planning in what I read; agents embellish memories.
agent_relevance: Importance-triggered reflection is an existing replay-like job in an LLM agent loop.

source: Zhao et al. (2024) ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners
finding: Agent compares success/failure trajectories and edits a rule list with ADD, EDIT, UPVOTE, DOWNVOTE; rules plus retrieved examples both matter.
numbers: HotpotQA: ExpeL 40% at R3 vs Reflexion 39%. Retrieve-only 40.3 to 54.4%; ExpeL+Reflexion 54.5 to 60.4% (table). Beats ReAct on HotpotQA, ALFWorld, WebShop.
limits: Insight extraction used gpt-4; hallucinated insights possible; suboptimal successes can mislead rules.
agent_relevance: Template for the offline episodes-to-rules job, with vote-based pruning of rules.

source: Wang and Sun (2025) PI-LLM: proactive interference in LLMs (cited in SleepGate)
finding: Cited via Xie: retrieval accuracy falls log-linearly toward zero as stale key-value updates accumulate; instructions to ignore old values help only marginally.
numbers: As reported by Xie 2026; not verified.
limits: Second-hand; original not opened.
agent_relevance: Motivates removing superseded entries from memory.

source: Momennejad et al. (2018) offline replay supports planning (cited in Lee 2026)
finding: Cited via Lee et al.: neural evidence of offline replay during rest predicts better planning in humans.
numbers: None quoted.
limits: Second-hand; not opened.
agent_relevance: Human link for offline computation helping later choice.

source: Anthropic Dreams for Claude Managed Agents (2026 product, per secondary blog)
finding: Research-preview feature: takes a memory store plus 1 to 100 past sessions and writes a new store with duplicates merged, stale entries replaced, insights added. Secondary source only.
numbers: No benchmark numbers found.
limits: Product feature, not evaluated.
agent_relevance: Industry practice: a separate offline job writes a new store and leaves the original untouched.

source: Title clash note: two unrelated papers named 'Language Models Need Sleep' (Lee et al. v3 footnote)
finding: Lee et al. renamed their paper and say Behrouz et al. study RL, parameter expansion, distillation and synthetic data. The sleep label is used loosely.
numbers: None.
limits: Neither paper tests human active-systems effects such as spindle-slow-oscillation coupling.
agent_relevance: Do not treat the word sleep as evidence for any mechanism; check what is tested.

source: Coverage note: no LLM study found that tests the human active-systems paradigms (targeted memory reactivation, spindle coupling, schema-consistent consolidation) on a language model
finding: All LLM work found borrows the metaphor (fast store, slow offline store, forgetting, schema abstraction) and measures task benchmarks, not human-style effects.
numbers: About 14 papers screened; 12 with usable numbers.
limits: Absence from my searches only (WebSearch plus arXiv API; Semantic Scholar not used).
agent_relevance: Treat consolidation as engineering design, not as validated by sleep science.
